definition: Benevolent means kind and inclined to do good for others.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word benevolent. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know benevolent should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Ship's logs describe a benevolent captain who let stowaways work off their passage instead of handing them over at the next port.
Well-meaning is weaker than benevolent: a well-meaning neighbor merely intends good, even if he never acts, while a benevolent one actually does good for others again and again.
Saintly goes further than benevolent — it points to goodness past everyday human reach, while benevolent people do real good on an everyday scale.

Kindly is warmth of manner — a kindly voice, a kindly smile, gentleness in how someone treats you moment to moment. Benevolent reaches past manner to a standing drive: a benevolent person is already looking for good to do, and the record of deeds, not the tone, is the proof.

Goodhearted says a person's nature is warm and well-intentioned, and it stays true even when no help ever gets given — good instincts, kind wishes. Benevolent adds the motor: an inclination that keeps turning into actual good done for others, a pattern anyone can point to.
